slides.title: A pacing guide is the map, not the drive
slides.lede: It sets the destination for each week. It does not tell you minute by minute how to get there — that is your lesson plan.

cards.b: Which week, the real dates, and how many student days you actually get. A four-day week is not a five-day week.
The strand you are in, and the essential question the week is trying to answer.
The Nevada indicator the week is accountable to. This is the part that has to be defensible.
What students should be able to do on cue, and the activity that gets them there.
How you will know they got it. A checklist, an exit cue, an observation — something you can point at.
It is not a script, and it is not fixed. Weather, assemblies and one hard class all move it. Move it on purpose.

slides.title: One week, all the way across
slides.lede: One real week from the PE guide — the whole thing is at coachkenny.org/pacing, all six grades, with the spreadsheet to download. Read straight across the row.

steps.b: Object Control II — how do body position and force change control?
kick, pass, plant foot, follow-through — 1.2.2 and 2.2.1.
Kick and pass to a target with control. Anchor: kick through gates.
A kick/pass checklist. Science: force and motion.

slides.title: The year at a glance
slides.lede: 36 weeks, 163 student days, every Nevada K-2 and 3-5 indicator covered in its own band. Every quarter opens with a procedures reset, on purpose.

stages.b: Weeks 1-3 are policy, procedures and safety only — entry and exit, the freeze signal, boundaries, equipment homes. Then locomotor, balance and first object control.
Procedures reset in week 10. Kicking and striking, rhythm and pathways, then the first fitness unit and a semester integration week.
Procedures reset again in week 19. Jump rope, endurance, strength and flexibility, then invasion, target and striking games.
Reset at week 27 into cooperative challenges and active lifetime choices. Weeks 31-36 are field day practice — relays, accuracy, balance, team challenges, then the day itself.

slides.title: What consistency actually looks like
slides.lede: Two specialists can run completely different rooms and still be aligned. Alignment is about the destination and the evidence, not the drill.

cards.b: Visual cues, short turns, large and light equipment, one instruction at a time. Success is participation and a recognisable attempt.
Skills in combination, tactics they can put into words, feedback to a partner, and chances to lead a station.
Weeks 10, 19 and 27 each open with procedures again. Do not skip it because “they already know.” They do not, in January.
Space, equipment, rules, cues, and the movement itself. Change any of them so every student can participate — that is not lowering the standard.

slides.title: Three things to walk out with
slides.lede: Turn to the person next to you and check each other. Nobody leaves this room without the shortcut on their phone.

items: Shortcut is on your home screen.
Your partner watched you open it.
Every quarter reopens with a reset.
Ask before the week starts, not after.
Moving a week is fine — move it on purpose.
Standard and evidence first, activity second.
Bring it to the next specialist meeting.
